acceptance.evidence: The candidate fixture points bare HEAD at refs/heads/seed and both candidate runs reached attribution without the Git 2.55 clone warning becoming fatal. A probe using the exact Run-FixtureGit implementation ran git rev-parse on a definitely absent ref, printed the real fatal error, threw 'git fixture failed with exit 128', and exited 1.

Against 462403d the harness exited 1 on the required seat-new row: 'ref_seat_new violations= elsewhere=refs/heads/loop/other-seat=...,refs/heads/loop/seat-new=... seat_created=' followed by 'FAIL ref attribution rows'. The candidate -SkipAgent run exited 0, but both ordinary candidate runs exited 1 later on the unchanged cmd /c push route, so the required ordinary-harness exit 0 was not observed.
git diff --exit-code d67c5e7 0f816bb -- docs/loops/qa-driver-template-cursor/ exited 0 with no output; the product template is unchanged.
QA 202's other findings were explicitly out of scope because the r4 diff touches only the standalone harness and its developer handoff.

regressions: The ordinary harness did not exit 0 in either of two runs: the cmd /c sanctioned push row reported denial=False moved=False after the plain node row moved successfully.
gaps: The repeated cmd /c push-route failure is outside the r4 fixture delta but blocks the dispatch's explicit ordinary-harness exit-0 criterion.
notes: Local Windows PowerShell evidence only; no CI and no windows=true run. Host used Git 2.55.0.windows.3, Windows PowerShell 5.1, and Node v24.5.0; Node v22 remains the repository's tested version.
